rubriker.title: Caruana Clinches Titled Tuesday On Rest Day
rubriker._rss_content: Fabiano Caruana used the first rest day of the U.S. Championships to win Chess.com's Titled Tuesday on October 13, finishing on 9.5 points, half a point clear of Hikaru Nakamura and Nihal Sarin. I

rubriker.title: US Championships: Caruana climbs to the shared lead in the open, Lee takes the sole lead in the women's
rubriker._rss_content: Fabiano Caruana defeated Ray Robson in round four of the US Championship to join Wesley So in the lead on 3/4. Awonder Liang suffered his first defeat against Jeffery Xiong, while Hans Niemann also collected a full point. In the women's tournament, Alice Lee took the sole lead by beating 13-year-old Megan Paragua, while Irina Krush scored her second victory of the event, defeating Nazi Paikidze. | Photo: Lennart Ootes / Saint Louis Chess Club

rubriker.title: U.S. Championship: Round 4
rubriker._rss_content: Round 4 in Saint Louis on Monday produced a new co-leader in the open section, as Fabiano Caruana beat Ray Robson to join Wesley So on 3/4, while Jeffery Xiong knocked Awonder Liang out of the lead. In the women's section, Alice Lee beat overnight co-leader Megan Paragua to go clear on 3.5/4, her third straight win.

rubriker.title: FIDE General Assembly adopts resolution on shorter time controls
rubriker._rss_content: FIDE is preparing changes to the regulations governing shorter classical time controls following a General Assembly resolution based on a proposal from the Icelandic Chess Federation. The FIDE Council plans to make 60+30 a standard classical control without special approval, while considering broader use of 45+30. Limits on games per day and title norms would remain, with further consultation planned before decisions on more extensive changes to classical tournament regulations. | Photo: FIDE

rubriker.title: Bodhana in the Bundesliga
rubriker._rss_content: Bodhana Sivanandan made her debut in the Second Bundesliga this weekend, playing for the Hamburger SK's men's team. She is the youngest youngest player ever to play in the German Bundesliga, and the youngest WGM in history. Her score in the two games she played: 1½ points. Not bad for an 11-year-old girl. Before the matches she visited ChessBase in Hamburg and did some recordings for us.

rubriker.title: ChessEver Founder Calls Lichess "Communist"
rubriker._rss_content: Grandmaster Vasif Durarbayli, the founder of the live-chess app ChessEver, has set out how he sees the online chess landscape in a thread on X, describing Chess.com as the capitalist end of the spectrum and Lichess as the communist end, with ChessEver aiming for the middle.

rubriker.title: Record Participation at 6th Intercontinental Online Chess Championship for Prisoners
rubriker._rss_content: The 6th Intercontinental Online Chess Championship for Prisoners kicked off with 140 teams from 56 countries, a new participation record, with teams competing in men's, women's, and youth sections.

rubriker.title: Nikita Vitiugov Says His Playing Career Is Over
rubriker._rss_content: England's highest-rated player, Grandmaster Nikita Vitiugov, has said his playing career is over, explaining that once he stopped improving he was no longer willing to give chess less than everything.
